page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration allocates 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores utilizing simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 16 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4 GB per core, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache and 1 MB of L2 cache per core. Supported processor instruction sets include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external cloud block storage for persistent data volumes. Accelerated graphics processing is omitted, with zero GPUs attached to the instance. Network capabilities are defined by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, providing sufficient capacity for standard inter-service communication without dedicated public IPv4 addresses included by default.

Benchmarking data reveals distinct performance characteristics across execution profiles. Single-core compute capability is prominent, with stress-ng single-core testing reaching 3073.57, placing it within the top 25 percent of comparable systems. Multi-core operations and general system benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core (6150.83) and PassMark overall CPU (7545.19), demonstrate mid-tier performance. Memory bandwidth and cryptographic tasks also align with median expectations. Conversely, high-throughput scenarios, including Redis SET operations (5.7 million ops/sec), multi-threaded compression tasks, and static web serving throughput (5.45 GB/sec), register in the lower quartile.

Given its balanced resource profile, ecs.g8a.xlarge offers predictable operational capacity for general enterprise compute tasks. It is well matched to standard application hosting, internal development tools, staging pipelines, and modular microservices. However, workloads demanding high transactional database write speed, deep memory caching, or significant network I/O may encounter performance boundaries due to baseline network and memory subsystem limits.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 16 GB of memory maintaining a 1:4 compute-to-RAM ratio, and a 2 Gbps baseline network connection. The instance includes no local storage or GPUs, relying on external network volumes for persistent storage. Benchmark results show strong single-threaded compute efficiency positioned in the top 25 percent, while multi-core workloads, encryption tests, and general CPU scores remain in the median range. Highly concurrent database and web serving throughput reflect lower quartile results. Consequently, this server provides a balanced foundation for moderate business workloads, staging servers, microservices, and general application backends.
